title: RAW UNREVIEWED: write eight source words as shrinking vertical character columns with paid word endings
summary: Invented complete hand procedure: copy successive source words onto at most eight scratch rows, then transmit their vertical character columns. An explicit END retires a finished row; the reader reconstructs the original words in row order. No lexical dictionary, hidden answer table, copying instruction or native word meaning. This is unreviewed supply, not a selected or surviving Voynich candidate; known terminal and local column-size obligations are retained.

design.mechanism: Ragged column transposition of successive blocks of at most eight complete source words. Each output group carries exactly one next source character or END from every currently active row, in original row order. END removes that row from later groups. The first column itself declares the row count through its count of complete character units; no empty padded rows or size header is written.
design.unit: One printed group is one vertical character column, not one source word, source syllable or cache entry. Complete source paragraphs are separately framed messages. Every block except the last in a paragraph contains exactly eight source words; the last contains one through eight.
design.contrast: Unlike929, this transposes characters of multiple complete words and never separates row/column coordinates of individual letters. Unlike930, output groups have changing size and preserve source spaces through explicit row retirement. Unlike940, no remembered fragment receives a reference code and no source-word END/CONTINUE mark is appended to every group.
design.prediction: If a group contains a decoded units, of which e are END, the next group in that same block must contain exactly a-e units. A block closes only when every unit in its current group is END. Any later group starts the next block. Thus decoded unit counts cannot increase before a pure-END closing group. Every complete paragraph ends with a nonempty pure-END group. These consequences are conditional on a fixed carrier and complete group/framing binding, not native discoveries.
design.scope: Source-preserving artificial writer and prospective obligations only; no encoding experiment, statistics, historical source, native alphabet, target fit or meaning assignment.
design.input_contract: Nonempty source tokens separated by one source space, with explicit paragraph boundaries. Tokens use lowercase a-z or the listed auxiliary characters. Their capitalization, spelling, punctuation, order, negation and unresolved pronouns are copied exactly. Repeated whitespace and source physical lineation are outside this edition. Unlisted characters cause failure, not normalization. The reader must know the source language to understand the exactly reconstructed message.

working_carrier.status: Fixed artificial teaching assignment; not a discovered native key. It was designed after known927/940 failures and the prior y/r/l terminal obligations, so it has no independent confirmation status.
working_carrier.lowercase_rule: Source a-s use the nineteen ordinary signs in order. Source t-z use q followed by the first seven ordinary signs. A q without its selector is invalid.
working_carrier.auxiliary_rule: For zero-based auxiliary index j, write cfh followed by ordinary_signs[floor(j/8)] and ordinary_signs[j mod8]. Reject unused indices. Both selectors come from the first eight ordinary signs.
working_carrier.framing: cph, q and cfh are distinct from the nineteen ordinary signs. A unit is one ordinary sign, q+one selector, cfh+two selectors, or the single END cph. These alternatives are prefix-free. The twenty-two listed working drawings are atomic within this invented lesson only; multiletter labels such as ch are one drawing here. Group spaces never split a unit.
working_carrier.width_qualification: Character units have widths one, two or three working signs; END has width one. Monotonic decoded-unit count is compulsory. Monotonic printed glyph length does NOT follow for this carrier because the following character in a still-active row may need a wider unit. A constant-width carrier would impose that additional length condition, but is not silently substituted here.

write: At paragraph start take the next eight source tokens, or all remaining tokens if fewer. Put them in scratch rows in their original order. Each row is nonempty. Do not insert null padding for missing rows.

Start every row at its first source character. In row order, emit the carrier encoding of the next character from every active row. The resulting column is one visible output group. The first column therefore contains one through eight character units and no END.

For each subsequent column, an active row with another character emits that character. A row whose last character was emitted in the previous column emits END exactly once and then retires. Preserve the order of surviving rows. Write all contributions as one group.

When the last active rows emit END, the entire closing group consists of END signs. Only now begin the next eight-word block. A block of fewer than eight rows is permitted only as the last block of its paragraph.

Keep the paragraph boundary explicit. Wrap physical output lines only between complete groups, never reset rows at an ordinary line wrap, and never open a new block or message merely to avoid a failed local condition.
read: At paragraph start or immediately after a closed block, parse the next group into complete carrier units. Require one through eight character units and no END. Their count initializes that many ordered rows, each with its decoded first character.

For each following group require exactly one unit per active row. Append each character to its row; retire each row receiving END. Keep completed rows in their original places rather than outputting shorter words first.

If all active rows retire, emit the completed source words in original row order, with single spaces. If this block had fewer than eight rows, require paragraph end. Otherwise another block may follow.

A paragraph ending while rows remain active is malformed. Unknown carrier units, too few or too many units in a column, an empty first group, a first-column END or an incomplete character escape are errors. No dictionary or plaintext oracle resolves them.
Retain paragraph boundaries exactly. Physical line wraps have no decoding effect.
design.single_unknown_repetition: A single-character source word emits its character in the first column and END in the next. Every new word follows the same spelling rule. Repeated source letters and complete source words are all retained. Identical consecutive output groups are legal when active rows next contain the same characters; no common initial header is forced. For example, eight rows all beginning with three copies of one source character produce three identical first columns, before any row ends. This is a symbolic construction statement, not an encoded manuscript or source test.
design.terminal_and_boundary_obligations: Ordinary columns may end in many ordinary character signs or END, not only two fixed finals. Nevertheless every completed block and message must end in a pure-END group. The parent has highlighted already known native complete-row/paragraph endings as a possible countercase: a multi-atom nonconstant terminal group cannot be pure END under any bijective sign renaming if it is independently bound as a complete message end. A physical line end alone is not such a binding. A native application would have to freeze actual visible paragraph/message boundaries before inspection; unmarked resets are forbidden.
design.known_local_countercase_obligation: Before this proposal was registered, the parent supplied the retained1208 f45r.10 mixed oky followed by longer kair as a possible local check. The writer must satisfy its exact decoded-unit recurrence there under any later declared binding. No native units were counted, no alternate carrier fitted, and no compatibility is claimed here. With a constant-width character carrier that sequence would additionally face the parent's monotone-length objection. The present variable-width lesson must not be retroactively modified if its unit recurrence fails.
design.learning_and_work: Learn26 lowercase encodings,56 auxiliary encodings, END, the prefix parsing rules and an eight-row writing routine. The writer needs lookahead of up to eight complete words or an eight-row scratch slate. The reader buffers up to eight complete words and their active/closed status, of unbounded total character length; this is NOT an eight-state or64-character memory claim. Reading cannot usually release a short word until longer earlier rows are resolved. The source alphabet, source-language knowledge, spelling effort and scratch-work are fully paid.
design.ink_cost: Every source character is transmitted once at its ordinary carrier cost, plus exactly one END per source word. Group spaces change, but no lexical abbreviation or ink compression is promised. No filler, secret dictionary, null cell or whole-message identifier is inserted.
design.smallest_falsifier: Before any source screen or key fitting, freeze a carrier and an already owned complete group window with its paragraph status. A nonclosing column followed by a column with the wrong complete-unit count rejects that binding. Independently, a complete-message ending that is not a pure-END group rejects it. No broad corpus search, new source or automatic repair is proposed.
design.structural_limits: Grouping depends jointly on several adjacent source words and can change output-group frequency cells; it is not one-word-one-code substitution. This is not evidence of a desirable distribution, directed components or GDT608 whole-form residual. It may produce conspicuous pure-END runs and large systematic changes of group size. Meaningfulness comes from exact recovery of ordinary source words, not from assigning native substring meanings.

predecessors_and_exposure.difference: General transposition is not new.929's one-word coordinate halves and fixed S-O-S contradiction remain. This design interleaves exact source characters from several words with variable active rows; it makes no row/column coordinate partition or R^n C^n claim.

No fixed semantic source grammar, concept lexicon or new semantic root. Ordinary source spelling and word order are preserved; all earlier fixed failures remain.

1201 proves transparent macro confluence on supplied symbolic primitives. This design instead fixes an exact invertible change from a natural source word stream to column groups, with explicit source-space and message recovery; no stable native primitive or content value is inherited.

1203 moves each source boundary by one character and fails its fixed source screen. Here letters of several words are reordered into vertical columns; this is not a different boundary-shift amount or repair.

No predecessor copying, cache reference or two-final group frame. Their conditional countercases remain. This proposal was knowingly designed after those failures and is not a pre-existing prediction or demonstrated survivor.
